solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S011-01.notes: Blueprints lost, layout inferred from cracks -> engineers could only conjecture (guess). verify contradicts 'could only'/'inferring'; dictate and recall don't fit. Medium because 'conjecture' is mid-level vocabulary.

S011-02.notes: Sentence 2 is the remembered image ('In his mind'); sentence 3 ('Now...') contradicts it. C describes sentence 3, a mild trap.

flags: minor: C and D are mirror images, so the per-resident direction is the only discriminator; A/B each give only half the data
S011-03.notes: $2.0M/100,000 = $20; $2.4M/150,000 = $16. Figures check out. Per-resident fall directly supports claim.

S011-04.notes: Distant stone plus almost no waste flakes -> tools were shaped elsewhere and arrived finished. B contradicts the missing flakes; C and D are unsupported.

S011-05.notes: Relative pronoun is the object of 'selected' (the committee selected her) -> whom. 'which' is for non-persons; 'who' is the common trap because the interrupting clause hides the object role.

flags: minor: correctness depends on reading 'several books' as making the title restrictive; some prep sources teach B as acceptable, so the key should cite the first sentence explicitly in the explanation
S011-06.notes: Carson wrote several books, so 'Silent Spring' is a restrictive appositive identifying which book: no commas around it. The comma after the title is needed to open the nonrestrictive participial phrase 'published in 1962,' which closes before 'drew'. B (commas around title) is the trap most test-takers pick; C/D break the phrase pairing.

S011-07.notes: Most sharks must swim; nurse sharks can rest motionless -> contrast.

flags: D is also defensible: it states the study's key finding verbatim from the notes. Only the phrase 'audience unfamiliar with the study' pushes toward A (which supplies context for the finding). Consider sharpening the goal (e.g., 'present the study's key finding along with the evidence supporting it') or rewriting D so it is clearly incomplete.
S011-08.notes: A gives both the evidence (crows scolded people in the trappers' mask) and the conclusion, which fits an unfamiliar audience; B and C give no finding; D gives the finding with no context.

flags: minor: correct choice C is the longest and most detailed choice
S011-09.notes: Common view (sudden break) -> Lindqvist disagrees -> her evidence (block printing, manuscript-like pages) -> her account (accelerated existing changes). Only one historian, so B and D are wrong.

flags: minor: C and D each give a plausible causal factor but don't explicitly link it to the loss; B is the only one with an attribution word, which test-wise solvers spot fast
S011-10.notes: Goal is to explain why the glaciers shrank; B gives the researchers' causal attribution (longer melt seasons) plus a detail. A states the effect only; C and D give facts without linking them to the loss.
